completion_data.completion_summary: Propagated the phase-closure and pre-edit-gate contracts from core's four implementer files to the non-core extension implementer surface (11 standard-mode agents, 2 hard-mode agents, 1 skill file) via the existing @-reference pointer-bullet convention, recorded two reasoned exclusions with grep evidence, generalized the three referrer-enumeration sentences in the contracts and context-layers.md, and passed a 7-assertion consistency/anti-copy-paste audit with zero .claude/ modifications and zero task-number citation leaks.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan's Context References list ends in a markdown table or a `---` separator rather than a plain bullet, append new pointer bullets directly after the last existing content line and before the next structural element (heading or separator) — do not invent a new subheading just to hold the appended bullets. Keeps additive diffs to exactly the specified lines with no extra structure.

For a source-store repo where agent-system/extensions/** is authoritative and .claude/** is a gitignored deploy artifact, `@`-reference bullet text in source-store files still names the deploy-time `.claude/context/...` path (not the source-store path) — this asymmetry is intentional, matching what gets deployed, and should not be corrected to the source-store path.

When auditing for prose-copy leaks via grep for distinctive contract phrases, a hit in a metadata/index file (e.g. index-entries.json's `summary` field) that predates the current task and isn't one of the task's actual edit targets is out of scope — distinguish index/registry metadata describing a contract from an actual consumer-file prose copy before treating a grep hit as a defect.
